d_sv_content.name: CAR T Cell Immunotherapy for Metastatic Osteosarcoma in Dogs
d_sv_content.tagline: Help us test a new treatment for advanced bone cancer in dogs.
d_sv_content.description:
This study is evaluating a new type of cancer treatment called CAR T cell therapy for dogs with osteosarcoma that has spread to the lungs.

CAR T cell therapy uses your dog’s own immune cells to help fight cancer. A blood sample is collected (about 3-4 tablespoons), and special immune cells (called T cells) are modified in a lab to better recognize and attack cancer cells. These upgraded cells are then given back to your dog through an IV infusion.

Dogs in this study will also receive medications to prepare the body for treatment and to support the immune system during the study. The goal is to determine if this treatment is safe and effective for dogs with metastatic bone cancer.
d_sv_content.requirements: Blood collection to create CAR T cells (about 2 weeks before treatment)Two days of pre-treatment chemotherapy before CAR T cell infusionOne IV infusion of CAR T cellsDaily oral medications throughout the studyRecheck visits on days 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, and 60 after treatmentExams, diagnostics, and blood collection at each visit
d_sv_content.responsibilities: Cover the cost of the initial exam and diagnostic testing for your pet’s cancerPay for exam fees at all study visitsBring your dog to all required appointments at CSUGive oral medications at home daily and keep a log of doses and any side effectsBe available for frequent follow-up visits over the 60-day study periodAll other study-related costs (including CAR T cell therapy, diagnostics, and lab work) will be covered by the study.
d_sv_content.whoCan: Dogs may qualify if they:Have osteosarcoma of the leg that that has been removed by surgeryHave cancer that has spread only to the lungs (visible on chest X-rays)Weigh at least 44 lbs (20 kg)Have adequate bloodworkHave not received chemotherapy within the past 2–3 weeksAre not receiving steroids or other immune-modifying drugsAre able to come to CSU for all study visits
d_sv_content.benefits: Benefits:Access to an advanced, experimental cancer treatmentStudy covers most treatment-related costs (except exam fees)Financial support available for screening testsUp to $2,000 coverage for treatment of study-related side effectsContribute to research that may improve cancer treatment for dogsRisks:Possible side effects from chemotherapy and immunotherapyRisks related to IV infusion and blood collectionTime commitment for multiple visitsTreatment may not be effective
d_sv_content.compensation: Owners cover initial diagnostics and exam fees; all study treatments and CAR T therapy are covered, with up to $2,000 for side effect care.
d_sv_content.timeCommitment: About 2 months with frequent visits (Days 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, and 60) plus daily at-home medications.
